sp.head.title: Starplast: gene evidence for Toxoplasma and Plasmodium
sp.head.description: Starplast {{STARPLAST_VERSION}}: a desktop app for exploring gene evidence in Toxoplasma gondii and Plasmodium falciparum: expression, fitness screens, localization, protein features, interactions and literature annotations.
sp.lede: Gene evidence for Toxoplasma gondii and Plasmodium falciparum in one place.
sp.prose: Starplast brings expression, fitness screens, localization, protein features, interactions and literature annotations together. Use it to look up a gene, investigate hits from a screen, compare groups of genes and choose candidates for follow-up experiments. The bundled maps contain 8,140 T. gondii genes and 5,720 P. falciparum genes, viewed separately.
sp.map.alt: Starplast gene map: thousands of points, one per gene, in coloured groups, with lines from one selected gene to related genes
sp.map.caption: The T. gondii gene map in Starplast's dark and light themes; it follows this page's theme. Each point is a gene; lines link the selected gene to related genes. Screenshots from the Starplast repository (MIT).
sp.does.title: What it does
sp.does.explore_text: Searches identifiers, symbols and descriptions, then shows the source evidence.
sp.does.predict_text: Compares held-out predictions before making calls for unlabelled genes, keeping related genes in the same evaluation group.
sp.does.compare_text: Joins a gene-level CSV or TSV to the existing evidence and keeps unresolved identifiers visible.
sp.does.strategies_text: Named ways of turning the combined data into a claim, each with a guide and a self-test against shuffled data.
sp.does.note: Positions on the map come from an embedding of selected features: nearby genes have similar inputs, which alone does not show a shared function or a physical interaction. Search scores help to prioritise candidates; they are not experimental validation. Gene tables and graphs ship with the package and work offline; 130 registered datasets are listed with their sources in the dataset catalogue.
sp.screen.title: Explore a screen
sp.screen.s1: Choose the organism under File → Species.
sp.screen.s2: Search for a gene ID. For T. gondii, File → Import data adds your screen results.
sp.screen.s3: Colour and filter the map by the measurements you want to compare.
sp.screen.s4: Click a gene to read its evidence and inspect each type of relationship separately.
sp.screen.s5: Select a group with a lasso or brush, then export the gene list for follow-up.
sp.install.title: Install Starplast {{STARPLAST_VERSION}}
sp.install.pip_note: Requires Python {{STARPLAST_REQUIRES}}, a display and OpenGL. Analyses run on the CPU; pip install "starplast[gpu]" adds NVIDIA GPU support on Linux x86-64 with a CUDA 12 driver.
sp.install.spacr_text: In the spaCR desktop app, the Starplast tile on the Toxoplasma page installs Starplast in its own Python environment and opens it as a separate application (marked alpha in spaCR). To look at spaCR results in Starplast, export a gene-level table from spaCR and import it with File → Import data.

mc.read.title: How to read these scores
mc.read.precision_recall: Precision is the share of objects the model reported that match a reference object; low precision means false detections. Recall is the share of reference objects the model found; low recall means missed objects.
mc.read.f1: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, so it is high only when both are. Either alone can look near-perfect: a model that reports one obvious object has high precision, and one that reports every dark blob has high recall.
mc.read.iou: IoU (intersection over union) is the overlap between a predicted and a reference object divided by the area the two cover together. F1 at IoU 0.5 counts an object as found when that ratio reaches 0.5.
mc.read.iou75: F1 at IoU 0.75 counts an object only when the ratio reaches 0.75, so the outline has to fit more closely.
mc.read.ap: Average precision at one IoU threshold is true positives divided by true positives, false positives and false negatives together. mAP averages it over several thresholds, so it also rewards outlines that fit closely.
mc.read.aji: AJI (aggregated Jaccard index) adds up the overlap of every matched pair and divides it by their combined area plus the area of unmatched objects, so merged, split and missed objects all lower it.
mc.read.dice: Dice is twice the overlap divided by the predicted area plus the reference area.
mc.read.map: mAP at IoU 0.5 is the mean average precision of the predicted boxes when a box counts as correct at an IoU (overlap divided by the area the two boxes cover together) of 0.5 or more. mAP at IoU 0.5 to 0.95 averages it over ten thresholds, so loosely placed boxes score lower.
mc.read.boxes: Precision is the share of predicted boxes that match a reference box; low precision means false boxes. Recall is the share of reference boxes the model found; low recall means missed wells.
mc.read.count: Median count error is the median difference between the predicted and the reference count per plate, as a percentage of the reference. Plates within 5% or 10% is the share of plates whose count error stays inside that limit.
mc.read.baseline: The grey bar is the baseline named in the column header, scored on the same test images: stock Cellpose-SAM without fine-tuning, or an earlier model where no stock model has the class.
mc.read.cv: Cross-validated scores split the data into folds, hold out each fold once and report the mean over folds with its standard deviation (SD). A single split can mislead; the SD shows how far the score moves from one split to another.
mc.read.heldout: The held-out test set is images kept out of training and used only for scoring.
